text: Director, Trabuco Canyon Water District
My wife and I have lived in Trabuco Canyon for over 25 years and raised our family here. Like many residents, my family has felt the impact of rising water costs.
Much of TCWD’s water and sewer infrastructure is decades old and requires significant reinvestment to maintain reliable service and protect public health.
With infrastructure costs rising, we must explore consolidation with SMWD and IRWD to determine whether economies of scale can provide meaningful, long-term rate relief.
As a water resources engineer with 30 years of experience and a master's degree in civil engineering from UC Irvine, I have the expertise to guide the district through the important decisions ahead.
I advocated repurposing underutilized district property for a potential OCFA firefighting helicopter facility to strengthen wildfire protection for our communities—at no cost to ratepayers.
It would be an honor to serve our community with the experience, urgency, and commitment it deserves.

text: Director, Trabuco Canyon Water District

As a Director of the Trabuco Canyon Water District, my highest priority is ensuring that our customers continue to receive safe, reliable, and responsibly managed water and sewer services. I am committed to supporting policies that maintain and upgrade our ageing infrastructure so the District can operate effectively for years to come.

In recent years, we have faced significant challenges-including state-mandated revenue reductions, a nationwide pandemic, and rising consulting and construction costs. Despite these pressures, I remain focused on keeping our water and sewer rates as low as practical while still protecting the reliability of our operations.

I believe the best way to serve our customers is to listen carefully to their input and make decisions that balance affordability with long-term reliability. Rate adjustments are an ongoing reality in today's environment, but I will continue seeking ways to offset costs through grant funding, operational efficiencies, and collaboration with neighboring water agencies.

While it may be tempting to promise rate reductions, I will not support commitments that jeopardize the District's ability to operate safely and dependably. Instead, I will continue working to keep rates as low as possible without compromising the reliability of the services our community depends on.

text: Professional Engineer/Educator

As a Trabuco Canyon resident, Engineer, and Father of three sons, I am committed to protecting the reliable water services and infrastructure our community depends on. I understand the importance of responsible leadership, long-term planning, and careful stewardship of ratepayer dollars.

Professionally, I bring 25 years of engineering and leadership experience managing complex technical programs, budgets, and schedules. As an Aerospace Engineering Manager and California-licensed Professional Engineer, I understand the importance of infrastructure reliability, preventative maintenance, risk management, and making sound investments that serve current and future needs.

I also serve as a U.S. Navy Reserve Commander and local educator. These roles have reinforced my commitment to accountability, transparency, and public service. My participation in this election does not imply endorsement by the Department of Defense.

As Director, I will prioritize reliable and affordable water service, responsible financial oversight, resilient infrastructure, emergency preparedness, and transparent decision-making. I will work collaboratively with fellow board members, district professionals, ratepayers, and community partners to address water supply challenges and plan responsibly for the future.

Together, we can protect our water resources, strengthen essential infrastructure, and ensure Trabuco Canyon Water District remains accountable, resilient, and responsive to the communities it serves.

text: Landuse Planner/Developer
As a concerned neighbor, I am running for the position of Trabuco Canyon Water District Director. Our community deserves a full board that puts efficiency, transparency, and long-term value first.

As an 18-year resident within the district, I have watched our water and sewer rates climb from ($85/month 2008 to $225/month 2026) and understand how that strains household budgets. My priority is straightforward: run this district as efficiently as possible so we can hold the line on costs, rather than passing every expense on to ratepayers.

I also support continuing the pursuit of consolidation with Santa Margarita Water District. Combining resources, staff, and infrastructure with a neighboring agency can eliminate duplicated overhead and create real economies of scale for savings that should pass directly back to residents.

Finally, I'm committed to real transparency. Ratepayers deserve clear, accessible information about how their money is spent, easy-to-follow board meetings, and a district that welcomes questions instead of deflecting them.
I am not a career politician — I'm someone who pays the same bills as you and want this district run responsibly, openly, and in service of the people it serves.
I would appreciate and value your vote this November.

text: CFO
I've called Trabuco Canyon home for 22 years, where my family has built our life and invested in this community.

As a CFO, I bring direct experience managing budgets, infrastructure investment, and long-term financial planning. Water districts face real pressures: aging infrastructure, rate sustainability, and environmental compliance. These aren't abstract issues; they affect every household's water bill and service reliability.

My background isn't theoretical. I've overseen capital allocation, vendor negotiations, and operational efficiency in complex organizations. Those skills translate directly to the boardroom: ensuring ratepayers get maximum value, prioritizing infrastructure investments correctly, and ensuring the district operates without waste.

I've also served this community for 20 years as a Little League coach, soccer coach, and board member of multiple nonprofits. That experience taught me to listen and represent what people need, not what I assume they want.
A board is only effective when it listens. Whether it's reliable service, predictable rates, or environmental stewardship, I will represent your interests.
Not every problem requires more spending; some require better decisions. That's where I can contribute.
I'm asking for your vote.

text: Financial Service Professional

For five years, I have been proud to call Trabuco Canyon home. Like many residents, I have watched our water and sewer bills rise sharply while families are asked to absorb repeated increases and growing long-term debt.

For more than 15 years as a financial service professional, I have helped families evaluate complex financial decisions, understand costs and risks, and choose solutions that protect their long-term interests. I will bring that same financial discipline, careful analysis, and accountability to the TCWD Board.

I support consolidation with Irvine Ranch Water District as the strongest path toward meaningful and lasting rate relief. Any final agreement must protect reliable service, responsibly address existing debt and infrastructure, and preserve fair representation for our community. This opportunity should be pursued with urgency and should not be undermined by unnecessary borrowing or financial commitments that could make consolidation more difficult.

As your Director, I will advocate for affordable rates, responsible budgeting, open communication, and full public disclosure before major decisions are made. I will ask tough questions, listen to residents, and put ratepayers first.
